academic_projects.name: Post-Quantum Security for Artemis zkML: Replacing KZG with FRI-Poseidon
academic_projects.tech_stack: Python, Qiskit, Solidity, FRI, Poseidon Hash, CP-SNARK
bullets: Identified critical quantum vulnerability in Artemis zkML framework: KZG polynomial commitments rely on ECDLP hardness, which Shor's algorithm solves in polynomial time

Demonstrated attack using BSGS recovering secret trapdoor in 52 microseconds (9-bit), 101ms (32-bit), and 10.9 hours (64-bit) on real MLP weights trained on MNIST (109,386 parameters); forged commitments accepted by verifier in all cases
Simulated Shor's algorithm using Qiskit Aer (24 qubits, 4096 shots) recovering trapdoor on 9-bit curve in 3.84 seconds, confirming quantum threat end-to-end
Designed and implemented post-quantum replacement substituting KZG with FRI-Poseidon, eliminating all elliptic curve dependencies across all 7 Artemis CP-SNARK commitment operations
Reduced commitment size from 64 bytes (ECC point) to 8 bytes (Merkle root); replacement requires no trusted setup and resists both classical BSGS and quantum Shor's attacks
